questions.problem: A linear transformation $T$ represents a dilation.  Given that $v=[\begin{aligned}60 \\ 144\end{aligned}]$ and $T(v)=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 12\end{aligned}],$ what is the standard matrix of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
We can write $T(v)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}\cdot [\begin{aligned}60 \\ 144\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}v\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $T(v)=\frac{1}{12}v,$ and so the linear transformation $T$ is a dilation with scale factor $k=\frac{1}{12}.$

The matrix that represents a dilation of scale factor $k$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 0 \\ 0 & k\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the standard matrix of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{12} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{12}\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Consider the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ of the Euclidean plane ${R}^{2}$ and the unit square spanned by the vectors, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/9e322e6ed1ddb8f1d094633e931cd179b7eb9d6f47acd7c7d0809f113df91b22.png)

Now, we compute the images of $\{i,j\}$ under $T$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =T(i)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-j \\ {j}^{′} & =T(j)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=-i\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following image:

Therefore, the matrix represents a reflection in the line $y=-x.$

What linear transformation is represented by the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/ec1286f66582da34b8b74c943ac6e473f1c18bebf5bc696b502a6aeb15cc013e.svg)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Consider the standard basis $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ and the unit square spanned by the vectors, as depicted below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/9e322e6ed1ddb8f1d094633e931cd179b7eb9d6f47acd7c7d0809f113df91b22.png)

We can find the images of $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =T(i)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=i \\ {j}^{′} & =T(j)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-j\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we obtain the following image:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/b93bb91dae85a3e3b40a8d0ade3d4f420064aaa6926431fa7f664c977bb8fd59.png)

Therefore, the matrix represents the reflection across the $x$-axis.

To visualize a reflection in the $x$-axis, consider the standard basis $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ and the unit square $\mathrm{R}$ spanned by the vectors, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/9e322e6ed1ddb8f1d094633e931cd179b7eb9d6f47acd7c7d0809f113df91b22.png)

We can find the images of $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =T(i)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=i \\ {j}^{′} & =T(j)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-j\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we obtain the following image:

tutorials.content:
A **reflection in the $x$-axis** is represented by the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/96d1e42ccb0e19c6a7fe605af0cbd17ded39967798c9804bf7514adc845c44b8.svg)

To visualize a reflection in the $x$-axis, consider the standard basis $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ and the unit square $\mathrm{R}$ spanned by the vectors, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/9e322e6ed1ddb8f1d094633e931cd179b7eb9d6f47acd7c7d0809f113df91b22.png)

We can find the images of $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =T(i)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=i \\ {j}^{′} & =T(j)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-j\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we obtain the following image:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/b93bb91dae85a3e3b40a8d0ade3d4f420064aaa6926431fa7f664c977bb8fd59.png)

Similarly, a **reflection in the $y$-axis** is represented by the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/40e77688a74462b8d0d29bca87db283c4ccb960fad6f1ac7cbac716a73f7b8e0.svg)

Again, we can find the images of $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =T(i)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=-i \\ {j}^{′} & =T(j)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=j\end{aligned}
$$

We obtain the following image:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/4993d8586a84e4a40a54edddd8011cd3d516264bfffc7e3c33d27a10edf1e7d7.png)

We can find the images of $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ under $T$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =T(i)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=j \\ {j}^{′} & =T(j)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=i\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we obtain the following image:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/0e37a258ea833a2d490fc34a34af40a5c7a18f7589f107c6d0ed631b331c8f2a.png)

Similarly, a **reflection in line $y=-x$** is represented by the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/f450c3581b23abb715ba02d7459b043f6414cbd06e50bafdafbdb011e4160625.svg)

We can find the images of $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =T(i)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-j \\ {j}^{′} & =T(j)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=-i\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we obtain the following image:

tutorials.content:
A **reflection in line $y=x$** is represented by the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/d6c5ff7f9c96510f6243059a023a32026a3ea0dd181a2b07bdf82147de887361.svg)

We can find the images of $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ under $T$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =T(i)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=j \\ {j}^{′} & =T(j)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=i\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we obtain the following image:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/0e37a258ea833a2d490fc34a34af40a5c7a18f7589f107c6d0ed631b331c8f2a.png)

Similarly, a **reflection in line $y=-x$** is represented by the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/f450c3581b23abb715ba02d7459b043f6414cbd06e50bafdafbdb011e4160625.svg)

We can find the images of $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =T(i)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-j \\ {j}^{′} & =T(j)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=-i\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we obtain the following image:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242551/assets/4a83673a409fd2e5d33b0b5f743f57af08cfb27c38e312a636179102c2172b04.png)
